items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: She used to come around our house and fix breakfast for the kids and myself... We were all hanging out together.

ctx.x: No, this was on 44th Street. She used to come down when she was in town... She'd wake up early. Like, regardless of what time she went to bed, she'd be up by 9 or 10 o'clock. And she used to come around our house and fix breakfast for the kids and myself -- I had a girl and a boy then. We were all hanging out together. So she used to come by and take the kids out for breakfast or something, or fix breakfast for them and then take them out shopping with her. I couldn't afford to take them shopping every day, but…

So I told her, 'Look, Billie, I don't appreciate you taking the kids out and buying them a whole lot of things when I can't buy them, because some of the days when they want to go out and get something and you're not here, what am I going to do? I don't have no money to spend like that.' So she told me, she said, 'Well, little Brother, don't pay it no mind. I'm gonna spend my money like I want to.' Ha-ha! So I cracked up behind it. I said, 'Well, that's right. I can't tell you how to spend your money. It's your…
